concepts.def: Violence against civilians for political ends
Weapons of mass destruction — nuclear, biological, chemical
Pope (1978-2005) who promoted peace and dialogue

walkthroughs.body_html:
Terrorism uses violence against civilians to create fear.

It fails just war: no legitimate authority, no discrimination between combatants and civilians.

Christianity and Islam both condemn it. Qur'an 5:32: 'whoever kills a soul. it is as if he had slain mankind entirely.'

WMD include nuclear, biological and chemical weapons.

They cannot discriminate between combatants and civilians, so most religious thinkers say they can never be used justly.

Nuclear deterrence — owning them to prevent attack — divides Christians. Pope Francis condemned even possession in 2017.

Pope John Paul II survived an assassination attempt in 1981, forgave his attacker, and worked tirelessly for peace — opposing the 2003 Iraq War.

The Quakers ran ambulance units in WW1. Bonhoeffer opposed Hitler. Desmond Tutu led South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission after apartheid.

These show religion at its best — promoting peace, forgiveness and reconciliation across divides.
